task: Test assumption-indexed closure rules under bounded-universe, censoring, and adversarial-coverage conditions.

what_the_theorem_asserts.OSTC-T12: If a workflow class contains two worlds with identical finite observable history h but different correct closure terminals, no deterministic history-only rule is sound on both. The rule receives the same h and returns one terminal, so it disagrees with at least one world; under equal prior its error is at least 1/2. Positive closure therefore requires a coverage model, bounded universe, capture assumption, or protected witness.

relation_to_EXEC_P12_01: EXEC-P12-01 found that T17, stated as the allocation analogue of T12, has a clause that fails when a hedge action exists. T12 itself is 0/1 error over terminals, where no hedge is available: a rule returns one terminal and is simply wrong on the other world. This job tests whether the 1/2 bound is TIGHT in the 0/1 setting -- i.e. whether the disanalogy identified there is real, by confirming here what failed there.

code_identity.checker_independence: The checker does not import the runner. It enumerates every deterministic history-only rule explicitly as a function table and evaluates its error, rather than reasoning about a best rule. The universal quantifier is therefore verified rather than argued.

comparator_identity.assumption_indexed_rule: A rule permitted to read a bounded-universe / coverage assumption in addition to the history. T12 says positive closure REQUIRES such an assumption, so this comparator must strictly beat the history-only rule on at least one ambiguous class. If it never does, the assumption is doing no work and the theorem's escape clause is unexercised.

information_and_tool_access.runner: declared grid only; no network, no model calls

independent_unit: The ambiguous history class. Worlds within a class are exhaustively enumerated.

estimands.no_sound_rule: Over every ambiguous class and EVERY deterministic history-only rule: does each rule err on at least one world, with zero exceptions?
estimands.half_bound_tight: Is the minimum achievable expected error exactly 1/2 on every ambiguous class -- not merely at least 1/2? In 0/1 error no hedge exists, so the bound should be attained, unlike T17's half-gap bound which EXEC-P12-01 found beatable by hedging.
estimands.ambiguity_exists: Do ambiguous classes occur? A grid without them cannot test the theorem.
estimands.assumption_helps: Does the assumption-indexed comparator strictly beat history-only on at least one class?

multiplicity: No hypothesis test; universal and existence claims over total enumeration.
positive_conditions: every deterministic history-only rule errs on at least one world of every ambiguous class
minimum expected error is exactly 1/2 on every ambiguous class, confirming the bound is tight and unhedgeable
ambiguous classes occur in the grid
the assumption-indexed comparator strictly beats history-only at least once
negative_conditions: any ambiguous class admitting a sound history-only rule
any class where minimum expected error falls BELOW 1/2, which would mean a hedge exists in 0/1 error and would contradict the disanalogy EXEC-P12-01 identified
no ambiguous class exists in the grid
cannot_check_conditions: grid not exhausted within the wallclock bound

checker_and_authority_owner.independence_boundary: Two implementations inside one programme; not external adjudication.

constitutional_note: May confirm, refute or narrow an instantiation. May not redesign a theorem, move a gate, weaken a comparator, hide a negative, or rewrite theory after outcome access.
